From Puckline Press

Puckline Press article

Frozen Frenzy, explained: the night all 32 NHL teams play

Tuesday's 16-game Frozen Frenzy was the fourth in a row. Here's what the event is, where it came from, how rare it is, and how last night went.

By Puckline Prince · Oct 14, 2026 · Article page

Read the article

Every NHL team played on Tuesday night. That's the Frozen Frenzy: one evening, 16 games, all 32 clubs, and a new puck drop almost every 15 minutes from 6 p.m. Eastern until the last game started at 11. ESPN says this was the fourth year in a row it has put the event on.

The Frozen Frenzy is a scheduling showcase built with ESPN. The league gives the night a full slate, then spreads the start times out so the games overlap as little as possible. ESPN carries a tripleheader on its main channel (6 p.m., 8:30 p.m. and 11 p.m. Eastern), and the other 13 games stream on its services.

The centrepiece is a whip-around studio show that jumps from rink to rink for goals, big hits and late finishes, the hockey version of the NFL's RedZone. In the first edition, John Buccigross and Kevin Weekes hosted it, and the show ran about six and a half hours across ESPN+ and ESPN2.

This year's tripleheader was Devils at Red Wings at 6, Avalanche at Stars at 8:30 and Bruins at Sharks at 11. The other games started every 15 minutes from 6:15 to 9 p.m., then at 9:45 (Flames at Ducks) and 10:30 (Oilers at Kings), so all 16 games had their own start time.

A night with all 32 teams in action is newer than you might think. The first 16-game day in NHL history was Saturday, April 8, 2023, the last Saturday of the 2022-23 regular season. That day started at 12:30 p.m. Eastern and was not branded as anything.

The first Frozen Frenzy came six months later, on Tuesday, Oct. 24, 2023. NHL.com called it the second 16-game day in league history. ESPN's tripleheader that night was Maple Leafs at Capitals, Bruins at Blackhawks (Connor Bedard's rookie season) and Flyers at the Golden Knights, the defending Stanley Cup champions.

Since then it has become a fixture of October:

  • Oct. 24, 2023: the first Frozen Frenzy
  • Oct. 22, 2024: opened with Capitals at Flyers, closed with Kings at Golden Knights
  • Oct. 28, 2025: opened with Penguins at Flyers, closed with Kings at Sharks
  • Oct. 13, 2026: opened with Devils at Red Wings, closed with Bruins at Sharks

All four have been on a Tuesday.

Nights like this are rare. Before the 2024 edition, NHL.com counted only three earlier days with all 32 teams playing: April 8, 2023, the first Frozen Frenzy, and Jan. 13, 2024. It also said the 2024 Frenzy would be the only day that season with every team in action.

So the Frenzy is the one guaranteed 16-game night on the calendar, and in some seasons it has been the only one.

The 2026 edition delivered 112 goals in 16 games, an average of seven a game. Road teams won nine of the 16. Three games went past regulation: the Devils won in overtime in Detroit, 5-4, and the Canadiens (over Buffalo, 4-3) and Kraken (in Philadelphia, 3-2) both won in shootouts.

All the final scores:

  • Devils 5, Red Wings 4 (OT)
  • Panthers 7, Blue Jackets 3
  • Canadiens 4, Sabres 3 (SO)
  • Hurricanes 4, Capitals 2
  • Kraken 3, Flyers 2 (SO)
  • Rangers 4, Lightning 1
  • Blues 7, Senators 2
  • Islanders 3, Canucks 2
  • Blackhawks 5, Penguins 3
  • Jets 5, Wild 2
  • Avalanche 3, Stars 2
  • Golden Knights 5, Predators 2
  • Mammoth 5, Maple Leafs 4
  • Flames 4, Ducks 2
  • Oilers 4, Kings 1
  • Bruins 6, Sharks 3

The most lopsided results were Florida's 7-3 win in Columbus and St. Louis's 7-2 win in Ottawa. In the 8:30 headliner, Colorado beat Dallas 3-2 in regulation, and Boston closed the night with six goals in San Jose.

Full recaps of every game are on the Last night page.

Sunday, November 8

Game recap

FLA3WSH4Final: FLA 3, WSH 4

Family night in Washington went to the Capitals, 4-3, and the Tkachuk brothers did everything they could to spoil it. Brady Tkachuk scored twice in the first period, both set up by Matthew, the second on the power play, for a 2-1 Florida lead. Then the Panthers stopped scoring and Washington didn't. Alex Tuch tied it with his 11th, unassisted, early in the second; Aliaksei Protas put the Caps ahead, and Pierre-Luc Dubois made it 4-2 early in the third, the two of them setting each other up like a buddy-cop movie. Jack St. Ivany had opened the scoring 2:21 in, also unassisted, because apparently nobody in red needed help. Tom Wilson's night lasted 2:13 and ended with 15 penalty minutes for boarding Sandis Vilmanis. Sam Bennett got one back with 47 seconds left and the goalie pulled. Logan Thompson made 27 saves, Akira Schmid 27 on 31. Matthew Tkachuk had three assists and still went home with nothing to show for them.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

STL1NSH3Final: STL 1, NSH 3

Nashville beat St. Louis 3-1, and Juuse Saros was the reason: 25 saves on 26 shots, with the only goal going in on a Blues power play. Jimmy Snuggerud scored that one, his ninth, midway through the first. Steven Stamkos answered on a Predators power play three minutes later for his 10th, and Ross Colton's goal at 9:02 of the second, set up by Jack Drury and Roman Josi, turned out to be the winner. Nick Perbix finished it into an empty net with 1:29 left. Joel Hofer was good at the other end, 26 saves on 28, which is the kind of night Blues goalies keep having: good enough to lose by two. Nashville is 8-4-5 and finally winning in regulation. St. Louis is 7-8-2, and its offense showed up for one power play and then went looking for the parking lot.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NYR4SEA3Final: NYR 4, SEA 3

The Rangers beat Seattle 4-3, which reads a lot closer than it was for 40 minutes. Gabe Perreault scored 95 seconds in, Tye Kartye added a power-play goal and Jaroslav Chmelar scored his first of the season, and Joey Daccord was on the bench after three goals on 10 shots in 13:53. Pavel Dorofeyev made it 4-0 in the second off Mika Zibanejad and Alexis Lafrenière. Then the Kraken remembered they're a hockey team: Kaapo Kakko, Jordan Eberle on the power play and Vince Dunn at 15:02 of the third pulled them within one. Joonas Korpisalo held the rest, 25 saves on 28. Philipp Grubauer stopped 15 of 16 in relief. Adam Fox picked up his 20th assist in 18 games, faster than any Rangers defenseman ever, Brian Leetch included. New York is 10-7-1. Seattle is 9-6-1 and has now perfected the art of the third-period comeback that starts about 20 minutes too late.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

MTL4TOR2Final: MTL 4, TOR 2

Montreal won 4-2 in Toronto, and the Leafs' coach spent part of it teaching a rookie a lesson in front of the home crowd. Alex Newhook scored twice in the first period for a 2-0 lead. In the second, Chris Kreider picked off Gavin McKenna's pass and scored on a breakaway for 3-0, and Hiller sat McKenna for the rest of the period. To his credit, McKenna came back and scored in the third, 55 seconds after William Nylander's power-play goal, and suddenly it was 3-2. Zachary Bolduc answered on the power play at 12:15 to end the drama. Jacob Fowler made 26 saves on 28; Sergei Bobrovsky stopped 24 of 28. The Canadiens are 11-3-3 and look like they're having fun. The Leafs are 8-8-2 with four regulation losses in five games, which in Toronto counts as a five-alarm fire and a full week of radio.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

UTA2OTT4Final: UTA 2, OTT 4

Ottawa beat Utah 4-2 with a late winner, and Samuel Ersson was the best player on the ice: 30 saves on 32 shots. Fabian Zetterlund put the Senators ahead on a first-period power play, Clayton Keller tied it four minutes later, and the game sat there until the third. Michael Amadio scored at 6:29, Barrett Hayton tied it again at 9:53 off Keller, and then Nick Cousins, of all people, scored the winner with 2:18 left, from Thomas Chabot and Shane Pinto. Pinto added the empty-netter at 19:44. Karel Vejmelka made 17 saves on 20. Ottawa is 11-6-1. Utah is 10-7-1 and outshot the Senators 32-21, which means the Mammoth did the heavy lifting all night and still got stuck with the bill.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NJD5NYI4OTFinal: NJD 5, NYI 4 OT

New Jersey beat the Islanders 5-4 in overtime after trailing 4-2 midway through the game, and the Islanders can't say they weren't warned: the Devils outshot them 50-23. Ilya Sorokin made 45 saves and still lost, which is about the cruelest thing that can happen to a goalie. Anthony Duclair, Matthew Schaefer, Simon Holmstrom and Victor Eklund scored for New York; Evan Rodrigues and Declan Chisholm kept New Jersey close. In the third, Luke Evangelista scored at 6:08 and Dougie Hamilton tied it on the power play at 13:42. Then Jack Hughes ended it 1:18 into overtime, assisted by his brother Luke. Jake Allen made 19 saves on 23 with Connor Hellebuyck getting the night off. The Devils are 12-5-0. The Islanders are 7-6-3 and spent 61 minutes proving that two-goal leads are just a suggestion.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CHI2CAR9Final: CHI 2, CAR 9

Carolina beat Chicago 9-2, and it was 7-0 after two periods, so the third was mostly paperwork. Jordan Martinook scored twice in the first, Andrei Svechnikov scored twice overall, and Seth Jarvis, Jackson Blake, Sebastian Aho, Alexander Nikishin and Shayne Gostisbehere all joined in. Nine goals tied the Hurricanes' record for a game since they left Hartford. Spencer Knight was pulled after six goals on 17 shots; Arvid Soderblom gave up three more on 16. Pyotr Kochetkov made 18 saves and has won 11 of his first 12 starts, something only 10 other goalies have done. Connor Bedard set up Roman Kantserov and scored himself in the third, long after it mattered. The Hurricanes are 14-3-2. The Blackhawks are 4-13-1 after six straight losses and held a players-only meeting afterward. Chicago keeps buying the rebuild, and the house keeps winning.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

SJS3DAL4Final: SJS 3, DAL 4

Dallas beat San Jose 4-3, and three power-play goals did it. Michael Misa scored first for the Sharks, then Roope Hintz on the power play, Jamie Benn at even strength and Jason Robertson on another power play made it 3-1 Dallas in the first. Benn's goal was his 999th career point, so Dallas fans get to do this all over again. Ivar Stenberg pulled San Jose within one early in the second, Thomas Harley's power-play one-timer made it 4-2, and Will Smith answered on a Sharks power play 2:32 later. Nobody scored in the third. Jake Oettinger made 20 saves on 23, Alex Nedeljkovic 26 on 30. Macklin Celebrini had three assists. The Stars are 10-5-2. The Sharks are 7-11-1, with a penalty kill that let in three goals on a night they lost by one, which is how you lose a hockey game while doing everything else right.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

TBL4MIN3OTFinal: TBL 4, MIN 3 OT

Tampa Bay was down 3-1 in Minnesota with about 13 minutes left and won 4-3 in overtime, with the winner scored by the guy who reportedly wants out of town. Blake Coleman and Maxim Shabanov scored early for the Wild, Jake Guentzel answered on a second-period power play, and Shabanov made it 3-1 at 6:49 of the third. Then Guentzel scored again at 13:44, Charle-Edouard D'Astous tied it at 16:29 with the goalie pulled on a power play, and Nikita Kucherov ended it 3:23 into overtime on another power play. So much for a quiet farewell tour. Dennis Hildeby made 19 saves on 22; Calvin Pickard stopped 30 of 34. Marcus Foligno and Scott Sabourin fought in the first. Tampa is 11-3-2 and plays in Winnipeg tonight. Minnesota is 12-3-4, still first in the Central, and found out a two-goal lead in the third doesn't come with a warranty.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

DET0COL4Final: DET 0, COL 4

Colorado shut out Detroit 4-0, and Mackenzie Blackwood didn't have to do anything fancy: 27 saves, all of them, against a Red Wings team that never found the net. Martin Necas and Nathan MacKinnon scored on power plays 2:44 apart in the second period, Necas added another at 7:15 of the third, and Cale Makar finished it on yet another power play at 9:45, three goals with the extra man in all. Necas finished with four points, Makar with three and MacKinnon with a goal and two assists. Gabriel Landeskog and Moritz Seider fought in the third, which was the most success Detroit had all night. Daniil Tarasov made 25 saves on 29. The Avalanche are 10-6-2. The Red Wings are 7-8-3, with their captain suspended and the team still looking for him in its offense.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

PIT5LAK2Final: PIT 5, LAK 2

Pittsburgh won 5-2 in Los Angeles, and Sidney Crosby made some history in the building where Marcel Dionne's jersey hangs. Crosby scored twice, the second into an empty net, to pass Dionne for sixth on the NHL's career points list. Tommy Novak got things going with two goals in the first 5:10. Corey Perry got one back for the Kings, Egor Chinakhov scored on the power play, and Alex Laferriere made it 3-2 on a Kings power play early in the second, but Crosby's first goal, late in the second, put it away. Evgeni Malkin had three assists. Sergei Murashov made 26 saves on 28 for his first win of the season; Darcy Kuemper stopped 14 of 18. The Penguins are 6-9-2 and in Anaheim tonight. The Kings are 5-8-2 and just watched a 39-year-old pass a franchise icon on their own ice, which is a lot to ask of a fan base already paying for this roster.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

VAN2EDM4Final: VAN 2, EDM 4

Edmonton beat Vancouver 4-2, and Connor McDavid had three more assists, stretching his season-opening assist streak to 18 games, tied with Adam Oates for the second-longest in NHL history. Leon Draisaitl scored twice, on the power play and into the empty net, and now has 16 goals. Mattias Ekholm opened the scoring, Max Sasson tied it with nine seconds left in the first, and Jason Dickinson put Edmonton ahead 49 seconds into the third. Brock Boeser made it 3-2 with the goalie pulled at 17:25 before Draisaitl iced it. Devon Levi made 20 saves on 22 in his return; Leevi Meriläinen stopped 26 of 29. The Oilers are 12-3-3. The Canucks are 3-15-1 with seven points, and at this rate the only thing they'll lead the league in is mock drafts.

Game recap

CBJ2BUF5Final: CBJ 2, BUF 5

Buffalo beat Columbus 5-2, and this one was settled by the middle of the second period. Josh Doan made it 5-1 at 10:53 of the second, and the rest of the night was a formality. Josh Norris scored twice, Jack Quinn opened it with his ninth, and Rasmus Dahlin added one. Owen Power had three assists and ran the game from the back end like he owned the building. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen stopped 24 of 26. Jet Greaves faced 37 shots and stopped 32, the hockey version of working a double and going home broke. Kent Johnson had a goal and an assist for the Blue Jackets, and Zach Werenski's power-play goal with 1:39 left was strictly for the fantasy crowd. The Sabres are 8-5-3. Columbus is 7-8-0, and its defense spent the second period watching Buffalo like it had paid for the tickets.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

SJS1MIN4Final: SJS 1, MIN 4

Kirill Kaprizov had four points, and Minnesota beat San Jose 4-1 to stay first in the Central at 12-3-3. Kaprizov opened the scoring on a first-period power play for his 16th goal, then set up the next three: Maxim Shabanov on another power play in the second, Quinn Hughes in the third and Zach Bogosian, his first of the season. Hughes played 31 minutes and finished with three points, so apparently nobody in St. Paul has told him about shift lengths. Jesper Wallstedt stopped 23 of 24, and the only one he missed was Macklin Celebrini's goal that tied it 1-1 in the second. Yaroslav Askarov made 25 saves on 29 shots. The Sharks have lost four straight and are 7-10-1. Their coach told them this week to ignore the noise, which was easy enough: the loudest thing in the building was the Wild's power play.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

ANA5CGY3Final: ANA 5, CGY 3

Anaheim does its best work from behind, and Calgary was kind enough to set the table. The Flames led 3-1 after one period on goals from William Stromgren, Joel Hanley and a Joel Farabee power play, and Lukas Dostal was pulled after giving up three on 11 shots. Ville Husso came in and stopped all 10 he saw, and the Ducks went to work: Tristan Luneau in the second, Leo Carlsson on the power play 55 seconds into the third, then Cutter Gauthier with the winner, his 12th, with 1:34 left. Nikita Nesterenko's empty-netter made it 5-3. Beckett Sennecke and Mikael Granlund had two assists each, and Dustin Wolf stopped 24 of 28. That's four straight wins for Anaheim, now 9-7-1. Calgary is 7-9-1 and just learned that a two-goal lead after 20 minutes is like a gift card: nice to have, gone by the weekend.

3
FinalCapital One Arena
4
Washington CapitalsWSH9-6-0 · 18 pts31 shots
1st2nd3rdTFLA2013WSH1214

Puckline's Report

Family night in Washington went to the Capitals, 4-3, and the Tkachuk brothers did everything they could to spoil it. Brady Tkachuk scored twice in the first period, both set up by Matthew, the second on the power play, for a 2-1 Florida lead. Then the Panthers stopped scoring and Washington didn't. Alex Tuch tied it with his 11th, unassisted, early in the second; Aliaksei Protas put the Caps ahead, and Pierre-Luc Dubois made it 4-2 early in the third, the two of them setting each other up like a buddy-cop movie. Jack St. Ivany had opened the scoring 2:21 in, also unassisted, because apparently nobody in red needed help. Tom Wilson's night lasted 2:13 and ended with 15 penalty minutes for boarding Sandis Vilmanis. Sam Bennett got one back with 47 seconds left and the goalie pulled. Logan Thompson made 27 saves, Akira Schmid 27 on 31. Matthew Tkachuk had three assists and still went home with nothing to show for them.

Puckline's Report

Nashville beat St. Louis 3-1, and Juuse Saros was the reason: 25 saves on 26 shots, with the only goal going in on a Blues power play. Jimmy Snuggerud scored that one, his ninth, midway through the first. Steven Stamkos answered on a Predators power play three minutes later for his 10th, and Ross Colton's goal at 9:02 of the second, set up by Jack Drury and Roman Josi, turned out to be the winner. Nick Perbix finished it into an empty net with 1:29 left. Joel Hofer was good at the other end, 26 saves on 28, which is the kind of night Blues goalies keep having: good enough to lose by two. Nashville is 8-4-5 and finally winning in regulation. St. Louis is 7-8-2, and its offense showed up for one power play and then went looking for the parking lot.

New York RangersNYR10-7-1 · 21 pts26 shots

Seattle KrakenSEA9-6-1 · 19 pts28 shots
1st2nd3rdTNYR3104SEA0033

Puckline's Report

The Rangers beat Seattle 4-3, which reads a lot closer than it was for 40 minutes. Gabe Perreault scored 95 seconds in, Tye Kartye added a power-play goal and Jaroslav Chmelar scored his first of the season, and Joey Daccord was on the bench after three goals on 10 shots in 13:53. Pavel Dorofeyev made it 4-0 in the second off Mika Zibanejad and Alexis Lafrenière. Then the Kraken remembered they're a hockey team: Kaapo Kakko, Jordan Eberle on the power play and Vince Dunn at 15:02 of the third pulled them within one. Joonas Korpisalo held the rest, 25 saves on 28. Philipp Grubauer stopped 15 of 16 in relief. Adam Fox picked up his 20th assist in 18 games, faster than any Rangers defenseman ever, Brian Leetch included. New York is 10-7-1. Seattle is 9-6-1 and has now perfected the art of the third-period comeback that starts about 20 minutes too late.

Puckline's Report

Montreal won 4-2 in Toronto, and the Leafs' coach spent part of it teaching a rookie a lesson in front of the home crowd. Alex Newhook scored twice in the first period for a 2-0 lead. In the second, Chris Kreider picked off Gavin McKenna's pass and scored on a breakaway for 3-0, and Hiller sat McKenna for the rest of the period. To his credit, McKenna came back and scored in the third, 55 seconds after William Nylander's power-play goal, and suddenly it was 3-2. Zachary Bolduc answered on the power play at 12:15 to end the drama. Jacob Fowler made 26 saves on 28; Sergei Bobrovsky stopped 24 of 28. The Canadiens are 11-3-3 and look like they're having fun. The Leafs are 8-8-2 with four regulation losses in five games, which in Toronto counts as a five-alarm fire and a full week of radio.

Puckline's Report

Ottawa beat Utah 4-2 with a late winner, and Samuel Ersson was the best player on the ice: 30 saves on 32 shots. Fabian Zetterlund put the Senators ahead on a first-period power play, Clayton Keller tied it four minutes later, and the game sat there until the third. Michael Amadio scored at 6:29, Barrett Hayton tied it again at 9:53 off Keller, and then Nick Cousins, of all people, scored the winner with 2:18 left, from Thomas Chabot and Shane Pinto. Pinto added the empty-netter at 19:44. Karel Vejmelka made 17 saves on 20. Ottawa is 11-6-1. Utah is 10-7-1 and outshot the Senators 32-21, which means the Mammoth did the heavy lifting all night and still got stuck with the bill.

Puckline's Report

New Jersey beat the Islanders 5-4 in overtime after trailing 4-2 midway through the game, and the Islanders can't say they weren't warned: the Devils outshot them 50-23. Ilya Sorokin made 45 saves and still lost, which is about the cruelest thing that can happen to a goalie. Anthony Duclair, Matthew Schaefer, Simon Holmstrom and Victor Eklund scored for New York; Evan Rodrigues and Declan Chisholm kept New Jersey close. In the third, Luke Evangelista scored at 6:08 and Dougie Hamilton tied it on the power play at 13:42. Then Jack Hughes ended it 1:18 into overtime, assisted by his brother Luke. Jake Allen made 19 saves on 23 with Connor Hellebuyck getting the night off. The Devils are 12-5-0. The Islanders are 7-6-3 and spent 61 minutes proving that two-goal leads are just a suggestion.

Puckline's Report

Carolina beat Chicago 9-2, and it was 7-0 after two periods, so the third was mostly paperwork. Jordan Martinook scored twice in the first, Andrei Svechnikov scored twice overall, and Seth Jarvis, Jackson Blake, Sebastian Aho, Alexander Nikishin and Shayne Gostisbehere all joined in. Nine goals tied the Hurricanes' record for a game since they left Hartford. Spencer Knight was pulled after six goals on 17 shots; Arvid Soderblom gave up three more on 16. Pyotr Kochetkov made 18 saves and has won 11 of his first 12 starts, something only 10 other goalies have done. Connor Bedard set up Roman Kantserov and scored himself in the third, long after it mattered. The Hurricanes are 14-3-2. The Blackhawks are 4-13-1 after six straight losses and held a players-only meeting afterward. Chicago keeps buying the rebuild, and the house keeps winning.

Puckline's Report

Dallas beat San Jose 4-3, and three power-play goals did it. Michael Misa scored first for the Sharks, then Roope Hintz on the power play, Jamie Benn at even strength and Jason Robertson on another power play made it 3-1 Dallas in the first. Benn's goal was his 999th career point, so Dallas fans get to do this all over again. Ivar Stenberg pulled San Jose within one early in the second, Thomas Harley's power-play one-timer made it 4-2, and Will Smith answered on a Sharks power play 2:32 later. Nobody scored in the third. Jake Oettinger made 20 saves on 23, Alex Nedeljkovic 26 on 30. Macklin Celebrini had three assists. The Stars are 10-5-2. The Sharks are 7-11-1, with a penalty kill that let in three goals on a night they lost by one, which is how you lose a hockey game while doing everything else right.

Puckline's Report

Tampa Bay was down 3-1 in Minnesota with about 13 minutes left and won 4-3 in overtime, with the winner scored by the guy who reportedly wants out of town. Blake Coleman and Maxim Shabanov scored early for the Wild, Jake Guentzel answered on a second-period power play, and Shabanov made it 3-1 at 6:49 of the third. Then Guentzel scored again at 13:44, Charle-Edouard D'Astous tied it at 16:29 with the goalie pulled on a power play, and Nikita Kucherov ended it 3:23 into overtime on another power play. So much for a quiet farewell tour. Dennis Hildeby made 19 saves on 22; Calvin Pickard stopped 30 of 34. Marcus Foligno and Scott Sabourin fought in the first. Tampa is 11-3-2 and plays in Winnipeg tonight. Minnesota is 12-3-4, still first in the Central, and found out a two-goal lead in the third doesn't come with a warranty.

Puckline's Report

Colorado shut out Detroit 4-0, and Mackenzie Blackwood didn't have to do anything fancy: 27 saves, all of them, against a Red Wings team that never found the net. Martin Necas and Nathan MacKinnon scored on power plays 2:44 apart in the second period, Necas added another at 7:15 of the third, and Cale Makar finished it on yet another power play at 9:45, three goals with the extra man in all. Necas finished with four points, Makar with three and MacKinnon with a goal and two assists. Gabriel Landeskog and Moritz Seider fought in the third, which was the most success Detroit had all night. Daniil Tarasov made 25 saves on 29. The Avalanche are 10-6-2. The Red Wings are 7-8-3, with their captain suspended and the team still looking for him in its offense.

Puckline's Report

Pittsburgh won 5-2 in Los Angeles, and Sidney Crosby made some history in the building where Marcel Dionne's jersey hangs. Crosby scored twice, the second into an empty net, to pass Dionne for sixth on the NHL's career points list. Tommy Novak got things going with two goals in the first 5:10. Corey Perry got one back for the Kings, Egor Chinakhov scored on the power play, and Alex Laferriere made it 3-2 on a Kings power play early in the second, but Crosby's first goal, late in the second, put it away. Evgeni Malkin had three assists. Sergei Murashov made 26 saves on 28 for his first win of the season; Darcy Kuemper stopped 14 of 18. The Penguins are 6-9-2 and in Anaheim tonight. The Kings are 5-8-2 and just watched a 39-year-old pass a franchise icon on their own ice, which is a lot to ask of a fan base already paying for this roster.

Puckline's Report

Edmonton beat Vancouver 4-2, and Connor McDavid had three more assists, stretching his season-opening assist streak to 18 games, tied with Adam Oates for the second-longest in NHL history. Leon Draisaitl scored twice, on the power play and into the empty net, and now has 16 goals. Mattias Ekholm opened the scoring, Max Sasson tied it with nine seconds left in the first, and Jason Dickinson put Edmonton ahead 49 seconds into the third. Brock Boeser made it 3-2 with the goalie pulled at 17:25 before Draisaitl iced it. Devon Levi made 20 saves on 22 in his return; Leevi Meriläinen stopped 26 of 29. The Oilers are 12-3-3. The Canucks are 3-15-1 with seven points, and at this rate the only thing they'll lead the league in is mock drafts.

FLA @ BOS · 1:00 PM ET

Florida PanthersFLA9-6-2 · 20 PTSML +122
@1:00 PM ETSun Nov 8 · TD Garden
FLA +122MLBOS -146
Boston BruinsBOS12-4-1 · 25 PTSML -146

Puckline Preview

Florida is back in Boston, and the last two springs these teams met, the Panthers sent the Bruins home: a first-round stunner in 2023 and a second-round exit in 2024. This one's a 1 PM matinee on the second night of a back-to-back for Florida, who lost 4-3 in Washington on Saturday and are running out of forwards. Aleksander Barkov, Brad Marchand (yes, the ex-Bruins captain, now in red, still out with a knee), Anton Lundell and Sandis Vilmanis are all out, so Jack Devine comes up from Charlotte. What they do have is the Tkachuk family business: Brady scored twice last night, both set up by Matthew, who added a third assist on Sam Bennett's late goal.

Boston is 12-4-1 with three straight wins, the last a 6-2 laugher in Pittsburgh, but lost rookie James Hagens (tied for the rookie scoring lead) to IR for a few weeks. Mikey Eyssimont comes up from Providence with 13 goals in 8 AHL games, which is either a hot streak or a sign the AHL needs better goalies. Jacob Markstrom gets the Florida net, and Jeremy Swayman (8-3-1, .912) is projected for Boston. It's the first meeting of the season, and Boston fans have had two years to work on their material.

By Puckline Prince

VGK @ BUF · 3:30 PM ET

Vegas Golden KnightsVGK11-5-2 · 24 PTSML -113
@3:30 PM ETSun Nov 8 · KeyBank Center
VGK -113MLBUF -106
Buffalo SabresBUF8-5-3 · 19 PTSML -106

Puckline Preview

Vegas wraps up a four-game road trip in Buffalo with points in all three games so far: a shootout loss in Boston, then wins in Pittsburgh and Detroit, the last on Trevor Connelly's late winner. The Golden Knights are 11-5-2 and 5-2-2 on the road, the rare tourists who leave town with more than they came with. Jack Eichel leads them with 23 points.

Buffalo is 8-5-3 and has won four of five, most recently 5-2 over Columbus on Friday behind two goals from Josh Norris and three assists from Owen Power. Jiri Kulich is back from a concussion and on the power play, while Ryan McLeod sits as a healthy scratch for a second straight game. The catch: the Sabres are 3-4-0 at home, so KeyBank Center has been friendlier to visitors than to its own team. Colten Ellis is expected to start as Buffalo keeps rotating him with Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen, and Adin Hill is projected for Vegas. It's the first meeting of the season, at 3:30, so Buffalo has all afternoon to prove the home record is a fluke.

By Puckline Prince

TBL @ WPG · 6:00 PM ET

Tampa Bay LightningTBL11-3-2 · 24 PTSML -150
@6:00 PM ETSun Nov 8 · Canada Life Centre
TBL -150MLWPG +125
Winnipeg JetsWPG6-8-3 · 15 PTSML +125

Puckline Preview

Tampa Bay rolls into Winnipeg on the back half of a back-to-back, fresh off erasing a 3-1 third-period deficit in Minnesota and winning 4-3 in overtime on Nikita Kucherov's power-play goal. That's the same Kucherov whose agent says his relationship with the Lightning is probably beyond repair, and Elliotte Friedman reports that people close to him say the wish to leave is sincere. Neither is confirmed by the team. Wherever he ends up, he'll miss the Jets: 31 points in 25 career games against them. Brayden Point hit 700 career points last night, and Tampa is 11-3-2.

Winnipeg is 6-8-3 and has won two straight after a nine-game winless run, the latest 6-2 over Vancouver on Thursday. The last time these two met, Oct. 29, Tampa won 6-4 for Winnipeg's seventh straight loss. Josh Morrissey skated in a regular jersey, but Scott Arniel says he won't play tonight, and the Jets are 3-8-2 since he went down. Andrei Vasilevskiy is projected after Dennis Hildeby started in Minnesota; Stuart Skinner is projected for the Jets, who have been off since Thursday. Life after Hellebuyck has been a lot of shots and a lot of praying.

By Puckline Prince

NJD @ TOR · 7:00 PM ET

New Jersey DevilsNJD12-5-0 · 24 PTSML -154
@7:00 PM ETSun Nov 8 · Scotiabank Arena
NJD -154MLTOR +128
Toronto Maple LeafsTOR8-8-2 · 18 PTSML +128

Puckline Preview

New Jersey visits Toronto on the second night of a back-to-back, and the Devils are rolling: 12-5-0, four straight wins and 8-1-0 in their last nine. The last three have all gone past regulation, including Saturday, when they came back from 4-2 down on Long Island and Jack Hughes won it in overtime, his third overtime winner of the season. Connor Hellebuyck appears to be starting, per the Toronto Sun, before his first trip back to Winnipeg on Tuesday.

The Leafs are in a mood. They're 8-8-2, seventh in the Atlantic, with four losses in five, and Saturday's 4-2 loss to Montreal cost them Morgan Rielly, who left with a lower-body injury; TSN expects Dakota Mermis to draw in. The same game had Hiller benching Gavin McKenna after his turnover gave Chris Kreider a breakaway goal. McKenna came back and scored, which is the most Toronto way possible to win a news cycle and lose a hockey game. Auston Matthews has points in 13 of his last 15, and Anthony Stolarz gets the net. The last time these two met, on Mar. 4, New Jersey won 4-3 in a shootout. Toronto fans would settle for any kind of win right now, shootouts included.

By Puckline Prince

PHI @ CGY · 7:00 PM ET

Philadelphia FlyersPHI4-10-4 · 12 PTSML -118
@7:00 PM ETSun Nov 8 · Scotiabank Saddledome
PHI -118MLCGY -102
Calgary FlamesCGY7-9-1 · 15 PTSML -102

Puckline Preview

The Flyers are 4-10-4 and 1-6-1 on the road, and they've scored two goals in each of their last two games, the second a 3-2 loss at Madison Square Garden. So Rick Tocchet shuffled the deck at practice, putting Porter Martone back with Matvei Michkov and Noah Cates. Michkov has eight goals in his last 10 games and says he wants more ice time, which is a bold ask on a team that could use more of everything. Dan Vladar is projected, but nobody has named a starter, and Philadelphia plays in Vancouver on Monday, so the goalies will likely split the weekend.

Calgary is 7-9-1 but 5-3-0 at home, and blew a 3-1 lead Friday in a 5-3 loss to Anaheim. Joel Hanley scored after stepping in on short notice for Kevin Bahl, who ruptured his Achilles in the warmup and needs season-ending surgery; Brayden Pachal comes up from the Wranglers. Joel Farabee leads the Flames with 16 points, and Devin Cooley is projected in goal after missing five games. First meeting of the season, between two teams whose fans have learned to enjoy the little things, like a shot on goal.

By Puckline Prince

PIT @ ANA · 8:00 PM ET

Pittsburgh PenguinsPIT6-9-2 · 14 PTSML +100
@8:00 PM ETSun Nov 8 · Honda Center
PIT +100MLANA -120
Anaheim DucksANA9-7-1 · 19 PTSML -120

Puckline Preview

Pittsburgh gets to Anaheim on the second night of a back-to-back, still glowing from a 5-2 win in Los Angeles that ended a four-game slide (0-3-1). Sidney Crosby scored twice there to pass Marcel Dionne for sixth on the NHL's career points list, Tommy Novak scored two of his own on a new line with Ben Kindel and Egor Chinakhov, and Evgeni Malkin had three assists. Sergei Murashov started that one, so Arturs Silovs is projected tonight. The Penguins are 6-9-2.

The Ducks are 9-7-1 with four straight wins and five or more goals in seven straight games. Cutter Gauthier has 10 goals in his last five games, a first in franchise history, and Jackson LaCombe has a nine-game point streak, the longest ever by a Ducks defenseman. The fine print: over their last 10 games they've allowed goals as fast as they score them, about 4.2 a night each way, and they're 2-4-1 at home. Ville Husso is projected after stopping all 10 shots in relief of Lukas Dostal on Friday, though nobody has said so. Troy Terry is back in full practice but hasn't made his season debut. First meeting of the season, and Anaheim's defense is still looking for its own.

By Puckline Prince
